goals.en:
Upon the successful completion of this course, students will be able to:
- Understand the relationship between events, patterns and system behavior in the Earth System their role in Earth’s resilience to global change (e.g., feedback processes) – CLO A
- Describe Earth’s energy balance and how it drives weather – CLO B
- Explain the general global atmospheric circulation patterns (e.g., large scale winds) and the reason behind them – CLO C
- Evaluate the global cycles of water and carbon with a particular appreciation of the different (slower and quicker) timescales involved in mass transfer between different sources and pools – CLO D
- Identify how anthropogenic impacts affect earth system components and dynamics across components – CLO E
- Apply the basic principles of modelling and systems thinking to natural systems – CLO F

description.en:
The Earth System course provides students with a solid grounding in the dynamics of our planet. Special attention is paid to the pressing environmental challenges facing the 21st Century. The course provides the necessary concepts and analytical tools to link specific local issues to a global framework. The course lectures will be supplemented by practical exercises and a group project where you will further research a current environmental issue and present your findings. 

In particular, the course will address the following Sustainable Development Goals: 

6- Clean Water and Sanitation 
7- Affordable and Clean Energy 
13- Climate Action 
14- Life Below Water 
15- Life on Land

This foundation course provides the theoretical basis for understanding the Earth as an interconnected system and the skills to use systems thinking as a tool to explore/assess/collaborate on complex problems. The course is connected to other courses by setting the physical boundaries and connection across the planet earth which provides the ground for the critical analysis of concepts like sustainability, innovation and governance, while introducing practical methodological tools, namely modelling and systems thinking, to examine complex issues across scales, perspectives and disciplines. In particular, the course prepares students for the Major in Energy, Ecology and Climate. The course relates to the SDGs by exploring the inner workings of different components of the Earth system (biosphere, atmosphere, lithosphere, cryosphere and hydrosphere) and their interactions. 

Active learning:  Earth System Science is about understanding processes, which is attained by active learning, i.e., by doing exercises, calculations, and exploring topics in assignments
